refs/rfc/rfc9110.txt 15.5.4: 'The 403 (Forbidden) status code indicates that the server understood the request but refuses to fulfill it.' ... 'The client MAY repeat the request with new or different credentials. However, a request might be forbidden for reasons unrelated to the credentials.' 15.5.2: 401 'lacks valid authentication credentials'. JwtTokenService.cs:20 puts customerId in sub, so a new token for the same customer carries the same sub. Lesson's conditioned wording ('When the refusal is about ownership') fits.

refs aspnetcore/security/authorization/resource-based.md:16: 'Attribute evaluation occurs before data binding and before execution of any method that loads a resource. Declarative authorization with an [Authorize] attribute doesn't suffice for resource-based authorization. Instead, the app must invoke a custom authorization method'. security/authentication/index.md:44: 'Calling UseAuthentication registers the middleware ... Call UseAuthentication before any middleware that depends on users being authenticated.' Program.cs:70 app.UseAuthentication().

Conditioned ('one way'). Code supports it: EfOrderRepository.ListByCustomerAsync filters Where(o => o.CustomerId == customerId), so rows of other customers are never loaded; live /api/v1/orders returned only customer 1's orders (claim 5).

Live (round 3): 'Authorization: Bearer abc.def.ghi' -> GET /api/v1/orders = 401, GET /api/v1/orders/3 = 200. No-header GET /api/v1/orders = 401. Matches [Authorize] on List (line 49) and none on Get (line 30). Also supports section 6: customer 1's token -> /orders/1 200 {"id":1,"customerId":1,...} and /orders/3 200 {"id":3,"customerId":2,...}. Docs opened this round: refs/rfc/rfc9110.txt, refs/aspnetcore-docs resource-based.md and authentication/index.md.

issues.quote: with the caller's `sub` — the claim in the token that holds the caller's customer id.

issues.quote: An ownership check here would do exactly that comparison after the `NotFound()` line — together with `[Authorize]`, so that there is always a caller to compare with — and answer `403` when they differ — that code does not exist yet, so this describes what should happen, not what happens today.

issues.fix: Split into two sentences: end the first after "answer `403` when they differ." and start a new one: "That code does not exist yet, so this describes what should happen, not what happens today."
